title: Oncall quick-playbook: API degradations and run-time failures
content:
Purpose:

A compact first-touch playbook for SREs responding to the four most frequent API failure patterns we observe in production: client-visible request timeouts (including backend RPC timeouts), sudden 429 storms, degraded or truncated streaming responses, and spikes in 5xx/error rates. The intent is rapid triage, safe short-term mitigations, and clear handoff to the owning teams for RCA and fixes.

Immediate first 5 minutes (what to say and do):
- Post a one-line incident summary to #prod-incident and #sre-oncall: symptom, affected region/routes, start time, whether paging escalation is needed.
- Record the incident start time in the ticket and capture 1 example request ID and client timestamp.
- Open these dashboards: api-latency-by-route (p95/p99), api-errors-by-code, serving-queue-depth, streaming-connections, model-worker-utilization.

Symptom triage matrix (quick):
- Timeouts (504/timeout)
  - Check: Is p95/p99 latency rising at gateway or at model-inference layer?
  - Typical causes: model worker tail latency, queue stall, network intermittency, long prefix processing.
- 429s
  - Check: Are 429s concentrated at the gateway or returned from model pool? Inspect rate-limit rules and per-tenant quotas.
  - Typical causes: misapplied rate-limit policy, client retry amplification, sudden traffic burst, quota translation bug.
- Degraded streaming
  - Check: Are SSE/TCP connections staying open? Look at last-chunk-time and chunk-interval histograms.
  - Typical causes: proxy idle/keepalive settings, head-of-line blocking in workers, kernel/IO regression in runtime.
- Elevated 5xx
  - Check: Error codes breakdown, error messages in logs, crashloop/restarts among workers.
  - Typical causes: memory leaks, dependency failures (auth, kv-store), corrupted model artifacts, recent deploys.

Fast, low-risk mitigations (apply immediately if safe):
- For timeouts:
  - Temporarily route traffic to a lower-latency model variant (small-quantized) using admin routing toggle. Record the change.
  - Shorten proxy backend timeout for affected route to prevent worker threads from being pinned by long tails (forces fail-fast).
- For 429 storms:
  - If the 429s are caused by a deployed policy, rollback that policy. If not possible quickly, relax soft quotas for impacted tenants via adminctl (record commands).
  - Introduce a short-lived global backoff header (X-Client-Backoff) via gateway config to slow client retries where supported.
- For streaming failures:
  - Flip endpoints to non-streaming chunked mode (deliver final response) if the client supports it.
  - Increase proxy keepalive and idle timeouts on the ingress (if we see connection resets).
- For elevated 5xx:
  - Drain and recycle affected worker pods, scale up additional workers to reduce queue length, and temporarily pause non-essential background jobs hitting the same pools.

What to inspect (20-60 minutes):
- Traces: find trace IDs for failing requests (gateway logs include X-Req-ID). Follow span timings to identify layer where latency/error is introduced.
- Logs: grep for repeated error patterns: "rpc timeout to model-worker", "kv cache miss exceeded", "OOMKilled", "connection reset by peer".
- Metrics: p95/p99 latency by service, queue length, worker utilization, request success ratio over 1m/5m windows.
- Infra: kube events (evictions, OOMs, restart counts), autoscaler decisions, cloud provider quota exhaustion messages.

Useful commands (examples):
- kubectl -n prod get pods -o wide | egrep "model|runtime"
- gcloud logging read "resource.type=gae_app AND severity>=ERROR AND textPayload:timeout" --limit=200
- PromQL for 429 by route: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"api-gateway\",code=\"429\"}[5m])) by (route)
- Queue depth: max_over_time(serving_queue_length[10m])

Streaming-specific checks:
- Inspect ingress access logs for status codes and connection_length. If resets appear at the proxy layer, adjust ALB/NLB/Envoy timeouts.
- Check runtime kernel and IO stats on worker VMs for increased syscall latency (e.g., iowait, context switches).
- Look for head-of-line blocking caused by long prefix processing or synchronous IO inside the model process.

Mitigation examples (exact commands to record in ticket):
- Route to small variant: PATCH /admin/models/<model_id> { "active_variant": "small-v1" }
- Relax tenant quota: adminctl quota update --tenant TENANT_ID --soft 2000
- Set ingress idle: kubectl -n istio patch configmap envoy-config -p '...idle_timeout: 5m...'
- Drain & restart pool: kubectl -n prod delete pod <pod-name> --grace-period=30

When to escalate immediately:
- Region-wide >25-30% failure rate sustained for more than 10 minutes.
- High-impact customer SLA breaches or legal/compliance signal.
- Evidence of data corruption, large-scale incorrect outputs, or security incidents.

Communication cadence and handoff:
- Updates every 10-15m while mitigation in progress, move to 30m during RCA.
- Primary on-call SRE owns coordination; paging serving-runtime lead if deep model/runtime debugging required.
- Notify Product & CS before any mitigation that reduces model quality.

Post-incident follow-up checklist (deliverables):
- Timeline with exact timestamps and list of affected customers.
- Collected traces and representative logs attached to the incident.
- Root cause hypothesis and confidence level.
- Concrete action items: code fixes, policy guardrails, alert tuning, and owners with target dates.
- Add automated canary for streaming chunk pacing (if not present).

Common root causes we have hit historically:
- Rate-limit policy translation bugs causing unexpected tenant throttles.
- Autoscaler metric mismatch (queue length vs CPU) leading to slow scaling.
- Memory leak in model runtime causing gradual worker death and 5xx spike.
- Client retry amplification creating feedback loops and saturating gateway.

Open proposals (next steps):
- Add synthetic streaming canaries that validate chunk frequency and connection liveness (owner: Lena).
- Auto-pin traffic to stable variants when p99 latency crosses threshold (proposal PR #812).
- Improve request-id propagation to ensure gateway assigns X-Request-ID before auth.

Quick notes to on-call: keep mitigation actions minimal and reversible. Document commands and approvals in the ticket. If you relax quotas or reduce model quality, call out the change in status notes and loop in product/CS.

References and recent incidents:
- SVC-INC-2025-07: 429 storm due to policy rollout; fix was rollback + quota relax.
- SVC-INC-2025-03: streaming stalls after runtime kernel upgrade; fix was kernel pin and patch release.

Contact list: oncall-sre@redwood.com, marcus.chen@redwood.com, lena.ortiz@redwood.com

End of playbook (draft) - A.P.
